definitions.explanation: Describes something extreme enough to constitute a record — most often used in news contexts about weather, heat, rainfall, sales figures, or other measurable values.

examples.japanese: {今年|ことし}の{夏|なつ}は{記録的|きろくてき}な{暑|あつ}さだった。
{記録的|きろくてき}な{大雨|おおあめ}で{道路|どうろ}が{冠水|かんすい}した。
{新製品|しんせいひん}は{発売|はつばい}から{一週間|いっしゅうかん}で{記録的|きろくてき}な{売上|うりあげ}を{達成|たっせい}した。
examples.english: Within a week of release, the new product achieved record-breaking sales.

notes:
Composed of {記録|きろく} (record) + {的|てき} (the adjectival suffix). Used as a na-adjective: {記録的|きろくてき}な + noun.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {記録的|きろくてき}な{暑|あつ}さ: record-breaking heat
- {記録的|きろくてき}な{大雨|おおあめ}: record rainfall
- {記録的|きろくてき}な{売上|うりあげ}: record sales
- {記録的|きろくてき}な{猛暑|もうしょ}: record-breaking heatwave

USAGE:
Strongly associated with news reporting, especially weather and economic figures. In conversation, native speakers often soften it with {過去|かこ}{最高|さいこう}の (highest ever) or {観測史上|かんそくしじょう}{最|もっと}も〜 (most ever on record) when speaking more carefully.
